findings.title: New public function Invoice.export_csv() has no test that references it
monthly_revenue now double-applies tax because it multiplies inv.total() by (1 + rate) even though total() itself now includes tax.
findings.detail: The docstring (line 7) states the assumption 'Invoice.total() is pre-tax, so tax is applied here', but after this PR total() returns subtotal * (1 + tax_rate). For any invoice with a nonzero tax_rate the contribution becomes subtotal * (1+rate)^2, so monthly revenue is taxed twice.

findings.title: apply_discount now computes the discount on the tax-inclusive total, so the same discount code produces a different total_override (and thus a different payable) than before for any invoice with a tax rate.
findings.detail: Line 34 sets total_override = self.total() * (1 - discount). total() previously returned the pre-tax subtotal and now returns subtotal * (1 + tax_rate), so the discount silently applies to tax as well; payable() (lines 18-20) returns this override, changing what discounted customers are charged.

findings.title: export_csv writes self.total() instead of self.payable(), so an invoice with an applied discount exports the pre-discount amount, contradicting the class's own definition of what the customer pays.
findings.detail: apply_discount (lines 30-36) sets total_override, and payable() (lines 16-20) is the method that returns the discounted amount; export_csv bypasses it and reports the raw total, producing a CSV that disagrees with payable() for any discounted invoice.
